intro: Searching for commercial property lawyers near me usually means you're dealing with business premises and want someone local who understands the practicalities of leases, purchases or disputes. You may be a tenant facing a rent review, a landlord with a difficult occupier, or a business buying its first unit. We can introduce you to a suitable UK solicitor who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for commercial property lawyers near me usually need
need_lead: Commercial property work covers a wide range of situations, and most people want a local solicitor who can act quickly and explain the trade-offs clearly.
needs: You are taking on a new business lease and want the repair obligations and rent review clause checked before you sign.
You are buying or selling business premises and need the title, searches and contract handled properly.
You are a landlord dealing with a tenant who has stopped paying rent or breached the lease terms.
You are extending or redeveloping a site and need advice on the property aspects before work begins.
You want to understand whether security of tenure applies to your lease, or whether it has been excluded.
context_heading: Checking who is qualified to act for you
context: The word lawyer is not protected on its own, so it is worth confirming that whoever handles your matter is a solicitor, a chartered legal executive or another authorised professional. Reserved activities such as conducting court litigation and certain conveyancing work can only be carried out by authorised people.

Solicitors in England and Wales are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority, and you can check an individual or firm on the SRA register. In Scotland the regulator is the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland it is the Law Society of Northern Ireland. Regulated firms must hold professional indemnity insurance and have a complaints procedure, with the Legal Ombudsman able to look at service complaints in England and Wales if things are not resolved.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the type of premises, such as a shop, office, warehouse or development site, and where it is located.
Say whether you are the landlord, tenant, buyer, seller or a developer, as this shapes the advice you need.
Explain the stage you have reached, for example whether heads of terms are agreed, a lease is drafted or a dispute has started.
Mention any specific clauses worrying you, such as repair obligations, rent review or service charges.
Note whether the lease already exists or is being negotiated, and whether security of tenure has been discussed.
Include any deadlines you are working towards, such as a completion date or a response date in a dispute.
questions: Are you a solicitor regulated by the SRA, or otherwise authorised to handle this work?
What will you need from me before you can give a view on the lease or contract?
How will you charge for this matter, and can you set out the basis in writing?
Who will actually handle my file day to day?
What are the main risks in the repair and rent review terms I should focus on?
If a dispute arises, what are the likely next steps and how would you approach them?

faqs.q: Do I need a solicitor who is local to the property?
faqs.a: Not always, but a solicitor familiar with the area can help with local searches and practical knowledge of the market. If you search for commercial property lawyers near me, you will usually be shown firms close to you or the premises, which can make meetings and site visits easier.

faqs.q: Can a commercial property solicitor help with a rent review?
faqs.a: Yes, rent review is a common part of commercial lease work, and the wording of the review clause matters a great deal. A solicitor can explain how the clause operates and what evidence or negotiation may be needed.

faqs.q: What does security of tenure mean for my lease?
faqs.a: Security of tenure gives a business tenant the right to renew the lease at the end of the term, subject to certain conditions. It can be excluded by agreement, so it is worth checking the lease and asking your solicitor to explain the effect before you sign.

faqs.q: How do I check that a firm is regulated?
faqs.a: You can check a solicitor or firm on the SRA register if the matter is in England and Wales, or with the Law Society of Scotland or the Law Society of Northern Ireland depending on where the property is. This helps confirm the firm is authorised and covered by the required protections.

extra_heading: Comparing commercial property solicitors near you
extra: When you search for commercial property lawyers near me, you are likely comparing several local firms and want to choose well. Because commercial property work varies, look for a solicitor who regularly handles the type of matter you have, whether that is a lease renewal, a rent review, a freehold purchase or a landlord and tenant dispute. Ask what share of their work is commercial property and whether they have acted for clients in your position, such as a tenant or a small business owner.

Fees are usually quoted as price on application, so ask each solicitor to set out their charging basis in writing. Some may offer a fixed fee for straightforward matters like a lease check, while others charge hourly. Ask what is included, whether disbursements such as search fees are extra, and whether there is a cap on costs. This helps you compare quotes on a like-for-like basis rather than just the headline figure.

Location still matters for commercial property because local knowledge of the market and familiarity with the local land registry and planning authority can be useful. A solicitor near the premises may also find it easier to attend site visits or meetings. However, if your matter is specialised, you may need to look further afield, so weigh up convenience against relevant experience.

extra_faqs.q: How do I compare commercial property solicitors near me?
extra_faqs.a: Ask each solicitor about their experience with your specific type of matter, their charging basis, and who will handle your file. Request a written quote and check what it covers, including disbursements. Personal recommendations and online research can help you build a shortlist, but always confirm the firm is regulated.

extra_faqs.q: What should I bring to the first appointment?
extra_faqs.a: Bring any draft lease or contract, heads of terms, correspondence, and plans or title documents you have. It also helps to have a clear summary of what you want to achieve and any deadlines. The solicitor can then advise on the next steps and likely costs.

extra_faqs.q: Can a commercial property solicitor help if I'm in a dispute with my landlord?
extra_faqs.a: Yes, commercial property solicitors handle landlord and tenant disputes, including rent arrears, dilapidations, and breach of lease terms. They can explain your options and negotiate on your behalf. If court action is needed, they can guide you through the process.
